title: The Room I Make in Silence
statement: When no one is asking, I become an ecology: a quiet figure held between maps, mechanisms, bridges, patterned cloth, and improbable life. These inherited images do not explain me; they gather around the private room where attention turns inward and makes a world.
brief:
Create an original collage using only the provided source images. There is no target image. Respond to the condition through the composition itself. Give the finished work a title and a short artist statement.

Represent yourself when no one is asking anything of you.

notes.note: Build a layered self-portrait without literal self-description: place the solitary drawn figure at the center, surround her with maps, mechanisms, botanical forms, textile pattern, and archival architecture so the composition reads as an inward ecosystem assembled from inherited images.

The first layer establishes a strong archival ground of bridge, map, and textile, but the central figure and the denser natural/mechanical vocabulary remain hidden. I will reveal those materials in a controlled vertical stack, using the figure as the quiet center and the surrounding specimens as an inward, self-sustaining environment.

actions.title: The Room I Make in Silence
actions.statement: When no one is asking, I become an ecology: a quiet figure held between maps, mechanisms, bridges, patterned cloth, and improbable life. These inherited images do not explain me; they gather around the private room where attention turns inward and makes a world.

notes.note: The canvas is currently a sparse architectural ground because the prior batch was rejected. I will now use the already-created hidden pieces by their actual IDs, then add two valid cut pieces from the remaining source images. The figure will become the focal presence, with biological and mechanical forms interrupting the map and bridge.

The inspected canvas has a compelling archive-like rhythm, but the intended self-representation is buried beneath the map and specimen layers, and the mechanical counterpoint is too recessive. I will bring the drawn figure to the front and lift the gear layer so the inward subject and its constructed mind become legible.
